To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of protostars forming by turbulent core fragmentation have resolved protostellar discs, but only very few of these discs are sufficiently extended to fragment.
turbulent cores are not necessarily turbulent during their collapse, that a significant fraction of the resulting protostars have accretion discs and that these discs do not necessarily fragment.
(i) turbulent flows are able to generate a significant amount of angular momentum in a collapsing core and (ii) the formation and fragmentation of discs is a rare event in turbulent cores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initial conditions for the formation of protoplanetary discs and planets.
the formation and early evolution of protostars in the context of the star formation process.
the formation of low-mass protostellar systems, and their evolution from the pre-stellar core phase to the protostellar phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of discs in the turbulent collapse of a pre-stellar core is a rare event.
the formation of a disc around a protostar is common (but not guaranteed), while the disc fragmentation and the formation of a binary system are rare events (but not impossible).
the formation of protostellar accreting discs in low-mass cores is a rare event, but it is not a rare event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a disc is not a sufficient condition for fragmentation, and that the presence of turbulence does not necessarily suppress the fragmentation of discs.
turbulent cores are more likely to form multiple protostellar systems with protostellar discs.
the formation of discs is not correlated with the angular momentum of the initial core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of a protostellar disc is a common occurrence for low-mass stars.
the formation of discs in turbulent cores is a common occurrence, but their fragmentation is rare.
the formation of protostellar accreting discs is not strongly correlated to the initial angular momentum of the core.
